derivations.claim: Rescaling the Hermite recurrence gives the position action; a norm-preserving phase rule on the dense finite span extends to a unitary using Hilbert completeness.
The only surviving ground-state coefficient yields the time-ordered oscillator correlator for positive and negative times.
Integration by parts on the two half-lines turns the derivative jump -i into the Feynman delta source.
The retarded kernel's derivative jump is +1 and its negative-time support differs from the correlator.
Subtracting an even cutoff isolates an integrable odd principal-value term and proves the real Plemelj limit.
The approximate-delta kernel has mass pi and a controlled tail, proving the imaginary Plemelj term and its sign.
Two convergent half-line exponential integrals yield the exact damped positive-sign Fourier transform.
Schwartz duality, Fubini, and the already-proved Plemelj limits justify the distributional boundary and its two opposite pole signs.

boundaries.evidence: Statement fixes the Hermite family indexed by n>=0, including normalized psi_0. The correlator is evaluated in that ground vector, so the detected word family does not quantify over an optional empty oscillator basis.
Steps 2.1 and 3.1 evaluate the kernel at t=0 and retain the derivative-jump delta there.
The construction is explicitly one mode and uses the ground state and first excited state in step 2.1.

boundaries.reason: The theorem assumes omega>0; omega=0 would collapse the two simple frequency poles and is outside the statement.

boundaries.evidence: Steps 3.1 and 3.2 compute the one-sided derivatives at t=0, the only joining point.
Step 1.1 carries AC_omega explicitly and applies the exact oscillator and Fourier supplier hypotheses.
